instructions: Dice the eggplants into 1/2-inch cubes. Dice the bell pepper, onion and tomatoes. Slice the garlic. Chop 2 tbsp of the parsley.
Heat 1/4 cup of the olive oil in a large deep skillet over high heat for about 1 minute, until it shimmers.
Add the eggplant and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Cook for 6 minutes, stirring often, until it's golden. Add the bell pepper and cook for 3 minutes, until it softens. Transfer everything to a serving bowl.
Put the pan back on high heat and add the rest of the olive oil. Add the tomatoes and onion and cook for 3 minutes, until the tomatoes break down.
Add the garlic, paprika, coriander, cumin seeds, 1/2 tsp of the pepper flakes, thyme and black pepper. Stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until it smells fragrant.
Add the vinegar, sugar, tomato paste and the remaining 3/4 tsp salt. Turn the heat to low and simmer for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce is thick and dark.
Spoon the sauce over the vegetables and sprinkle with the parsley.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve warm or at room temperature. Put the remaining 1/2 tsp pepper flakes on the table for anyone who wants heat.
method_notes: No version with 20 or more ratings could be read, so Cup of Yum's Turkish eggplant shakshuka (5 from 9 ratings) leads: fried eggplant and pepper set aside, then a spiced tomato sauce simmered thick and spooned over. Sprinkles and Sprouts (4.2 from 5) fries eggplant and zucchini and uses canned tomatoes. The lead's boiled potato is left out to save time. Half the pepper flakes move to the table to keep it mild.
